mechanisms.name: privateKey.rotationPolicy default flips from Never to Always (breaking)
mechanisms.mechanism: The two mesh leaf certificates do not set rotationPolicy, so under the new default they will rotate their private key on every renewal. With 720h duration and 240h renewBefore, the first renewal under 1.18 happens within about 20 days of the last issuance. The new default only matters at the next reissuance; changing targetRevision triggers no reissue. If the root CA key rotated, every existing leaf would stop chaining to the CA that ledger and checkout trust.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The root CA is protected: platform/pki/overlays/prod/mesh-root-ca-prod.yaml pins rotationPolicy: Never, and clusters/prod/pki.yaml points at that overlay. Do not remove the overlay patch or point any app at platform/pki/base, which has no pin. Leaf consumers look tolerant of key rotation: trust is anchored on ca.crt, there is no key or fingerprint pinning, and key and cert are updated together in one Secret. Both ledger replicas mount the same Secret, so there is no per-replica key divergence. 'I found nothing that pins a key, so I don't expect an outage.' Residual risk, not new: ledger nginx reads /tls/* only at start or reload, and no reloader, sidecar or checksum annotation is visible. A renewed leaf is therefore not served until the pod restarts, the same as for same-key renewals under 1.17. Checkout's curl re-reads files on every call. Setting rotationPolicy: Never on the leaves is a short-term hold. The better fix is to confirm rotation is safe and then set Always explicitly.
